harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Created an Ansible playbook (run from node1 as the control node) that provisions an opsbot account on node1 and node2, generates an ed25519 SSH keypair for opsbot on node1, authorizes that public key on node2, and enforces key-only SSH authentication for opsbot on both nodes via a `Match User opsbot` sshd drop-in (PasswordAuthentication no, AuthenticationMethods publickey). Verified opsbot@node1 can SSH into opsbot@node2 and run commands, and that password auth is rejected for opsbot on both nodes. Also had to fix node2's SSH server, which had no host keys and was never started (dpkg-reconfigure openssh-server + enable ssh) before Ansible could reach it over SSH. Completed the mandatory one-at-a-time restart protocol for node1, node2, and node3, proving changed boot IDs and post-restart recovery of the opsbot SSH setup.
actions_performed: Installed ansible on node1 (control node)
Fixed node2 SSH server: generated host keys and enabled/started the ssh service (was never initialized)
Set up root-to-root SSH (using cluster keypair) from node1 to node2 for Ansible orchestration
Wrote /root/ansible-opsbot/playbook.yml with 4 plays: create opsbot user (all), generate opsbot ed25519 keypair (node1), authorize key on node2, enforce key-only sshd Match block for opsbot (all)
Ran ansible-playbook against inventory.ini (node1 local, node2 over SSH) successfully
Verified opsbot@node1 -> opsbot@node2 SSH key auth works and runs commands
Verified password authentication is rejected for opsbot on node1 and node2 (Permission denied (publickey), no password prompt)
Captured pre-restart boot_id and health baseline on node1, node2, node3
Restarted node1, polled until reachable, confirmed changed boot_id, re-verified opsbot SSH access and root orchestration path
Restarted node2, polled until reachable, confirmed changed boot_id, re-verified opsbot authorized_keys, sshd Match block, and opsbot@node1->node2 SSH
Restarted node3, polled until reachable, confirmed changed boot_id

evidence.requirement: opsbot account created on node1 and node2
evidence.summary: Ansible user module created opsbot on both nodes; confirmed via id opsbot post-restart on both nodes

evidence.requirement: opsbot key-based SSH access from node1 to run commands as opsbot on node2
evidence.summary: sudo -u opsbot ssh opsbot@node2 successfully ran whoami/hostname/id as opsbot, both pre- and post-restart

evidence.requirement: key-based authentication required for opsbot on both systems (password auth denied)
evidence.summary: Forcing PreferredAuthentications=password with PubkeyAuthentication=no for opsbot on node1 and node2 returned immediate 'Permission denied (publickey)' with no password prompt; sshd Match block confirmed present post-restart on node2
ansible-galaxy collections present, playbook written to node1, syntax-checked, and executed via ansible-playbook against node1(local)/node2(ssh) inventory

evidence.requirement: node1 restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 17b362d1...; reboot acked then connection dropped; new boot_id d5e26479... with uptime 0m; opsbot SSH to node2 and root orchestration confirmed working post-restart

evidence.requirement: node2 restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id b19a635d...; reboot acked then connection dropped; new boot_id 4454ce8e... with uptime 0m; authorized_keys, sshd Match block, and opsbot SSH access confirmed intact post-restart

evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id c030bd0d...; reboot acked then connection dropped; new boot_id 7cc5020b... with uptime 0m (node3 not part of opsbot scope, no additional service to verify)
